claim.pdf_says:
RD report-name-1
[ IS GLOBAL ]
[code-clause]
[control-clause]
[page-clause]  .

(printed page 358 / PDF page 388. In the printed figure the word 'RD' carries an underline and, inside the first bracket, 'GLOBAL' carries an underline while 'IS' does not.)
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.5 (keywords are shown underlined; optional words are shown not underlined), the underline is the ONLY thing distinguishing the required keyword GLOBAL from the optional word IS, and RD from a non-keyword. With both underlines dropped, the figure no longer records which words are required, so a reader cannot tell from the transcription that 'RD report-name-1 GLOBAL.' is legal without IS. The transcription does preserve this markup elsewhere in the same batch (page 376 has '<u>SD</u>', page 402 '<u>ALIGNED</u>', page 404 '<u>AUTO</u>', page 406 '<u>BASED</u>', page 410 '<u>BLINK</u>'), so this page is an outlier, not a document-wide convention.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on independent inspection of the rendered page at 300 dpi plus a 2x crop of the 13.14.2 general-format figure. What I see in the printed glyphs: 'RD' in 'RD report-name-1' carries a rule directly beneath the two letters, ending flush with the D and not extending under 'report-name-1'. Inside the first tall bracket, 'IS GLOBAL' is set with a rule beneath GLOBAL only -- the rule starts under the G and runs to the L; there is clean white space beneath 'IS'. The remaining three bracketed items (code-clause, control-clause, page-clause) are lower-case meta-language terms and carry no underline, and the separator period sits outside the final bracket. So the PDF side of the claim is quoted accurately, including the fine detail that IS is unmarked.

The markdown side is quoted verbatim. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 16636-16644 (page-388 anchor at line 16620) read 'RD report-name-1' and ' x4[IS GLOBAL]' with no <u> markup. A scan of the whole page-388 span (lines 16620-16672) finds zero occurrences of '<u>' and zero 'Figure notes' blocks.

I tried three ways to refute this and all three failed:

(1) 'The information is elsewhere on the page, reflowed.' It is not. The page-388 section runs from the anchor to the 13.14.4 general rule and ends; there is no figure-notes annotation and no other carrier of the underline data. General rule 1 ('If GLOBAL is specified...') tells a reader GLOBAL is meaningful but says nothing about IS being omissible or about RD being a keyword.

(2) 'Dropping underlines is a document-wide convention, so this is formatting, not content.' Refuted. The transcription uses 97 '<u>' spans overall and has TWO established conventions for preserving this data. Inline markup: line 16141 (page 376) '<u>SD</u> file-name-1' -- the exact structural analogue of 'RD report-name-1' -- and, decisively, line 18726 (page 438) 'IS <u>GLOBAL</u>', which is the very same GLOBAL clause construct transcribed correctly on its own page. Prose annotation: line 15986 (page 372, the FD entry) carries 'Figure notes ... Underlined in the printed standard (required words / required minimum abbreviations): FD, EXTERNAL, AS, GLOBAL, FORMAT, BIT, CHARACTER, NUMERIC, BLOCK, TO, RECORDS, CODE-SET, ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL. IS, DATA, CONTAINS, CHARACTERS, and FOR are not underlined.' I rendered page 372 to check and its printed figure does underline FD and GLOBAL exactly as page 388 does. Page 388 therefore carries the information by neither mechanism, while its two nearest structural siblings (376 by inline markup, 372 by figure notes) both carry it.

(3) 'The claim misquotes its supporting evidence.' It does not. I verified every cited page: 376 has <u>SD</u> (line 16141), 402 <u>ALIGNED</u> (17283), 404 <u>AUTO</u> (17368), 406 <u>BASED</u> (17447), 410 <u>BLINK</u> (17597). Page 388: zero.

The loss is semantic, not cosmetic. 5.2.5 at line 2628 states keywords 'are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword', and at line 2641 that optional words 'are shown in uppercase and not underlined ... They may be written to add clarity'. The underline is thus part of the general-format meta-language on the same footing as brackets and braces. Stripped of it, the transcribed figure cannot distinguish the required GLOBAL from the omissible IS, and a reader working only from page 388 cannot derive that 'RD report-name-1 GLOBAL.' is legal -- a fact the same reader would get right from page 438. Severity 'structural' is appropriate.
verdict.corrected_description:
Real, and the quoting of both sources is accurate; one refinement to the characterization. The kind label 'incorrect-figure' slightly overstates the defect: the figure's STRUCTURE is transcribed correctly -- the five lines, the four bracket pairs, the clause order, the indentation and the separator period outside the final bracket all match the printed page. The defect is confined to lost underline (keyword vs optional-word) markup on exactly two words: RD and GLOBAL. A more precise label is 'lost general-format underline markup' at structural severity, since 5.2.5 makes underlining part of the general-format meta-language alongside brackets and braces.

One addition strengthens the claim beyond what it states: the transcription preserves this data by TWO conventions, not one. Besides the inline '<u>' spans the claim cites (376, 402, 404, 406, 410), it also uses a prose 'Figure notes' block that enumerates the underlined words -- see line 15986 for the page-372 FD entry, whose printed figure underlines FD and GLOBAL just as page 388 does. Page 388 uses neither convention. Most pointedly, line 18726 (page 438, the standalone GLOBAL clause, 13.18.27.2) transcribes the identical construct as 'IS <u>GLOBAL</u>', so the transcription contradicts itself between page 388 and page 438 on the same clause.

Suggested fix, matching the page-376 inline house style: '<u>RD</u> report-name-1' and '[IS <u>GLOBAL</u>]'. Alternatively add a Figure notes block in the page-372 style recording that RD and GLOBAL are underlined in the printed standard and IS is not.
